name.en: Grandparent scam: “I’m in trouble, please don’t tell Mom”

how.en: A caller says they are your grandchild or another relative, or a lawyer, police officer or doctor helping them. They say there was an arrest, a crash or another emergency, that it is urgent, that you are the only one who can help, and that you must keep it secret. Some scammers use AI to clone a relative’s voice from a short clip posted online. They ask for money by wire transfer, crypto, a payment app or gift cards.

text.en: A call or message from someone who sounds like your grandchild or another relative, or from their “lawyer”.
They say there was an arrest, a crash or a hospital stay and they need money right now.
They beg you not to tell their parents or anyone else.
They ask for bail or fees by wire transfer, crypto, a payment app or gift card numbers.
Grandma it’s me. I’m in trouble, I had an accident and the police are holding me. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad. My lawyer is going to call you about the bail, I need it today.

en: A relative in trouble who needs money right away.
They ask you to keep it secret, even from their parents.
A “lawyer” or “officer” takes over the call.
Payment by wire transfer, crypto, payment app or gift cards.
The voice sounds right but the story is new to you.
Hang up, or say you will call back. Then call your relative on a number you know is theirs.
If you can’t reach them, call another family member or a friend, even if you were told to keep it secret.
Ask a question only the real person would know, or agree a family secret word ahead of time.
If you already paid, contact the company you used to send the money right away.
